sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Orléans steers drivers towards car parks and keeps its on-street rules short and strict. The Métropole says it wants to cut solo car driving and favours long stays in car parks and short stays on the street, with on-street stays limited to 2 hours in the orange zone and 4 hours in the green and violet zones, and a 25-euro post-parking charge [15]. The charge rose from 17 to 25 euros on 1 January 2024, and from 12 February 2024 the free first 30 minutes ended in the car parks run by Orléans Gestion, except Münster and Aubrais, while the day rate was capped at 10 euros instead of 18.80, as announced in January 2024 [8]. On 19 May 2025 the city council unanimously approved on-street changes from 1 July 2025 of about 2% on average and resident permits from 21 to 22 euros a month, and the free 1h30 for electric cars ended [5]. The operator's tariff page of 21 October 2026 shows 0.50 euro per 15 minutes up to 1h30 and an 8-euro daily shopping rate [6].

The national mobility law forces another change: 565 parking spaces within 5 metres before pedestrian crossings must be removed across the metropolis by the end of 2026, 268 of them in Orléans, with works begun in June 2026 [12]. The city planned to add paid on-street parking near the station, about 30 spaces on the avenue de Paris and about 70 on rue des Sansonnières, and the metropolitan council gave a favourable opinion on the principle on 3 April 2025 [13]. In March 2024 the mayor reaffirmed his opposition to low-emission zones; the page does not show the current legal position [14]. Charging at the Métropole's own points was announced as priced at 0.50 euro per kWh from January 2024, after two free hours [16].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: Two projects change the supply. Orléans Métropole reported on 12 October 2026 that demolition of part of the Marie-Stuart shopping centre began in mid-October so the place Mozart car park can be extended with 12 extra spaces, with works due to finish in spring 2027 [0]. The Halles Charpenterie car park was listed for renovation in summer 2026, and the open-data feed on 21 October 2026 still flagged it as closed for works [1]. Beyond that, the Métropole's key-figures publication counts 3,505 regulated paid on-street spaces and 6,700 spaces in 16 closed car parks, without a year for those two figures, and puts Loire crossings at 95,000 vehicles a day in 2023, 12% below 2018 [17].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
Orléans Gestion, a public local company owned 52.15% by the Métropole and 47.85% by the city, runs 12 car parks in Orléans and Fleury-les-Aubrais with 5,766 spaces, as well as on-street parking with about 3,000 paid spaces [2]. According to council minutes of 3 April 2025 it has run 11 public car parks since 1 January 2023 under a concession to the end of 2032; Médiathèque and Cheval Rouge have separate contracts, and Martroi is conceded to Indigo until 2033 [3]. On 3 April 2025 the council approved a weighted rise of 2% in car park prices from 1 July 2025, and the rapporteur said 2024 revenue was 7.9 million euros, 70% from hourly parking [4]. The first two quarter-hours cost 0.70 euro at Cathédrale, Cheval Rouge, Danton, Hôtel de Ville and both Halles car parks and 0.60 at Carmes, Médiathèque, Patinoire and Saint-Paul, with a 10-euro day package and a 38 to 40-euro 7-day pass; Gare des Aubrais costs 0.20 euro per quarter-hour [7]. Indigo's Martroi page shows 0.60 euro for 15 minutes [9]. The open-data export lists 31 sites, 23 with live availability, including 12 tram park-and-rides under Effia and a Place d'Arc car park under 'Carrefour'; for Gare des Aubrais the feed puts the enclos under Effia while the council documents put it under Orléans Gestion [10][11].

Our data cover 13 car parks with 4,843 spaces that have at least two weeks of readings, from the metropolis feed, measured since 5 October 2026. Occupancy averaged about 44% on weekdays and 36% at weekends, weighted by spaces. The Cathédrale (343 spaces) is the fullest at 67% on weekdays, followed by Saint-Paul (234) at 65%, Patrimoine (434) at 61% and Médiathèque (410) at 60%; Cathédrale and Cheval Rouge reached full in single readings. The Place d'Arc car park (678) averaged 9%, Münster 29% and the Droits de l'Homme car park falls from 25% on weekdays to 2% at weekends. The Martroi garage appears for only three days. These are two and a half weeks of data.
